course.title: Content Creation & Portfolio
course.welcome: Make work with enough clarity, craft and character to earn a permanent place in your portfolio.
course.description: A practical studio course about building considered creative work, documenting your process and presenting it with confidence.

guestLecturers.name: Lina Åberg
guestLecturers.bio: Lina directs brand worlds and image systems for fashion, culture and hospitality clients. Her practice sits between strategy, styling and the small details that make a campaign feel intentional.
guestLecturers.lectureDescription: A candid walkthrough of how a loose visual instinct becomes a coherent creative campaign.
learningOutcomes: Translate references into a visual direction
Make production choices that protect the core idea

guestLecturers.name: Omar Said
guestLecturers.bio: Omar works across portraiture, editorial and brand storytelling. He is especially interested in the edit: the moment separate images become a point of view.
guestLecturers.lectureDescription: How to choose, sequence and present images so an audience understands both your work and your perspective.
learningOutcomes: Edit with a clear point of view

portfolioBriefs.title: Independent Eyewear
portfolioBriefs.shortDescription: Launch a characterful eyewear label for people who collect objects with stories.
portfolioBriefs.description: Create a focused launch campaign for an independent eyewear brand with a distinctive point of view. Your case should combine product, personality and a world the audience wants to enter.
portfolioBriefs.background: The brand has exceptional frames but little recognition outside a small design community.
portfolioBriefs.challenge: Turn a functional product into a cultural object without relying on luxury clichés.
portfolioBriefs.audience: Design-aware 25–40 year olds who value independent labels.
portfolioBriefs.creativeFreedom: High — choose the brand name, casting, location and medium.
portfolioBriefs.portfolioValue: Demonstrates art direction, styling, image making and campaign thinking.

portfolioBriefs.title: Premium Skincare
portfolioBriefs.shortDescription: Give a science-led skincare launch a warmer, more human point of view.
portfolioBriefs.description: Develop the launch concept for a skincare range that is clinically credible but emotionally distant. Build an image system that makes everyday care feel personal.
portfolioBriefs.background: The formulas work brilliantly, but the existing identity feels cold and interchangeable.
portfolioBriefs.challenge: Balance efficacy, sensoriality and trust in one cohesive launch story.
portfolioBriefs.creativeFreedom: Medium — retain a restrained, ingredient-led tone.
portfolioBriefs.portfolioValue: Shows concept development, product storytelling and visual consistency.

portfolioBriefs.title: Boutique Hotel
portfolioBriefs.shortDescription: Make a new coastal hotel feel like a place worth travelling for.
portfolioBriefs.description: Create a seasonal campaign for a small hotel whose strongest asset is atmosphere. The work should give potential guests a reason to linger, not just a reason to book.
portfolioBriefs.background: The property is beautiful, but its communication feels generic and location-led.
portfolioBriefs.challenge: Turn quiet moments, local rituals and hospitality into a memorable narrative.
portfolioBriefs.audience: Creative professionals seeking a slower weekend away.
portfolioBriefs.creativeFreedom: High — choose a season and the experiences you want to foreground.
portfolioBriefs.portfolioValue: Demonstrates editorial thinking, hospitality storytelling and cohesive presentation.

portfolioBriefs.title: Coffee Roastery
portfolioBriefs.shortDescription: Help a local roastery make its daily ritual more visible.
portfolioBriefs.description: Create a small but resonant content series for a coffee roastery that cares deeply about process, people and place.
portfolioBriefs.background: The coffee is excellent and the regulars are loyal, but its online presence has no distinct voice.
portfolioBriefs.challenge: Find a simple, repeatable content format that feels as considered as the product.
portfolioBriefs.audience: Local coffee drinkers and design-conscious visitors.
portfolioBriefs.creativeFreedom: High — work with image, motion, sound or text.
portfolioBriefs.portfolioValue: Shows restraint, consistency and a clear social-first idea.

groupProject.overview: Work in a small studio team to create a complete campaign concept for a fictional client. Your outcome is a concise, well-articulated creative response rather than a large volume of assets.
timeline: Week 2 — form teams and select a scenario
Week 8 — final presentation and process archive
deliverables: A visual system and hero assets
groupProject.assessment: We assess concept clarity, relevance to the audience, craft, collaboration and your ability to explain decisions.

faq.question: Can we use AI-generated imagery?
faq.answer: Yes, when it is appropriate to your idea and clearly documented in your process. The work still needs a visible point of view and thoughtful direction.

faq.question: How are groups formed?
faq.answer: You may form your own group of 3–4 people in week 2. Speak to your teacher if you need help finding a group.

scenarios.title: Premium Skincare
scenarios.shortDescription: Make clinical care feel quietly luxurious and personal.
scenarios.brief: A new skincare line wants to own the evening ritual. Create a launch campaign that makes performance feel intimate rather than technical.

scenarios.title: Boutique Hotel
scenarios.shortDescription: Give an under-the-radar hotel a reason to become a ritual.
scenarios.brief: Build a seasonal campaign around the feeling of checking out of everyday life without leaving your curiosity behind.

scenarios.title: Outdoor Lifestyle
scenarios.shortDescription: Reframe outdoor gear for a new, urban-minded audience.
scenarios.brief: Create a launch for a lightweight outdoor collection that belongs as naturally in a city as it does on a trail.

scenarios.title: AI Startup
scenarios.shortDescription: Make an ambitious creative tool feel understandable and useful.
scenarios.brief: Position a new AI tool for independent creative teams without lapsing into the usual technology visual language.

finalPortfolio.overview: Your final portfolio is an edited record of what you made, how you think and what kind of creative work you want to do more of.
structure: A clear landing page and short introduction
A contact page and relevant links
finalPortfolio.submission: Submit your portfolio URL and a PDF process archive in Canvas by 17:00 on 20 March.
finalPortfolio.assessment: We look for authorship, conceptual strength, visual quality, editing and your ability to make each project understandable to a new audience.

faq.question: Which platform should I use?
faq.answer: Use the platform that helps your work feel clear and easy to navigate. Framer, Readymag, Adobe Portfolio and a hand-built site are all welcome.

faq.question: Can I include work from before this course?
faq.answer: Yes. The final portfolio should be a truthful, edited picture of your current practice; label collaborative work clearly.
